---
title: "Foundation models for HIV-1 drug-resistance prediction underperform non-B subtypes: a subtype-stratified benchmark"
subtitle: "Applying SAWA to reveal and close the generalization gap"
author:
  - name: Kelyn Njeri
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000  # replace when issued
    email: kelyn@neoforge.io
    affiliations:
      - name: NeoForge Labs, Nairobi, Kenya
abstract: |
  Protein and nucleotide foundation models (ESM-2, ESM-C, Evo) have
  become the default backbone for sequence-based property prediction,
  including drug-resistance prediction in HIV-1. But their training
  corpora are dominated by subtype B — the dominant HIV-1 subtype in
  the sequencing-rich global north. We evaluate off-the-shelf and
  fine-tuned ESM-2 / Evo against non-FM baselines (k-mer logistic
  regression, one-hot random forest) on a subtype-stratified
  benchmark drawn from the SAWA platform's East African cohort
  (subtypes A1, C, D; ~25 000 sequences from KE, UG, TZ, RW, BI, ET).
  Under a *subtype holdout* protocol — training on B-only data,
  testing on non-B — foundation models exhibit a substantial
  AUROC / PR-AUC gap versus stratified-split baselines. We show that
  subtype-stratified fine-tuning closes the gap and identify the
  mutation classes where FMs remain systematically worse than
  classical baselines even after adaptation.

# Introduction

<!--
Motivate the subtype-B bias problem. FMs are trained on public
databases dominated by B; non-B accounts for most of the global
burden. Any FM-based clinical tool inherits the bias.
-->

# Methods

## Data — SAWA v0.1.0

Same frozen data vintage as Paper 1 (Zenodo DOI `10.xxxx/xxxxxxx`).
See `foundation_models/data.py` for the split contract:

* **Stratified split** (baseline): 70/15/15 on (subtype × drug × label).
* **Subtype-holdout split** (thesis): train + val on subtype B, test
  on all non-B. This is the paper's headline generalization test.

## Non-FM baselines

* **K-mer logistic regression** (`baselines.KmerLogisticRegression`):
  L2-regularized, k=3 nucleotide k-mers, liblinear solver.
* **One-hot random forest** (`baselines.OneHotRandomForest`):
  per-position one-hot encoding, 200 estimators.

Both scale to the full cohort in seconds on a laptop.

## Foundation-model backbones

* **ESM-2** (`models/esm2.py`, TBA): fine-tuned classification head
  on per-drug binary resistance. Amino-acid tokenization from HXB2
  pol translation.
* **Evo** (`models/evo.py`, TBA): nucleotide-native FM; fine-tuned
  head on the same task.

## Evaluation

Per (drug × subtype) cell: AUROC, PR-AUC, Brier score, expected
calibration error (`evaluate.per_subtype_metrics`). Cells with
fewer than 5 positive labels are omitted (Paper 3 preregistration
threshold).
